evidence.anchor: A revealed anchor reprice is a cancel-to-hidden rearm

summary: process_user_order ingests cumulative fill evidence before matching authenticated CANCELLED consumes a persisted rearm/terminal intent. Rearm uses the guarded atomic placement/logical status write; other cancellations must pass guarded status projection before cancellation replacement handling. A failed guard pauses and suppresses replacement while factual ingestion remains. Intentional project stops and duplicate terminal acknowledgements remain non-originating, and the source-SID factory guard closes the stop-versus-child-creation race.

cancel_order first resolves a managed stealth root or placement client_order_id and routes it through the same durable logical-stop command as cancel_stealth_order. Responses distinguish accepted stop from exchange_cancel_pending and copy committed state. The unmanaged fallback still tracks a raw REST cancel_orders(order_ids=[client_order_id]) call, with its separately recorded identifier hazard.

summary: place_order generates a client_order_id, normalizes limit price and size, performs a tracked REST create_order, classifies the response fail-closed, and emits an explicit success/error response.

Order/status/log mutations update shared engine_state under state_lock and enter a single 0.25-second-default rate-limited, coalescing latest-state publisher; slow dashboard clients have bounded send time and are disconnected. Ticker publication retains only the latest pending sample per product, spread windows use constant-space aggregates, and stealth snapshots periodically serialize manager memory. OrderEngine status samples RuntimeController coherently at its publication boundary, but normal shutdown stores DRAINING/false and later STOPPED is available through admin_status rather than republished engine status. Current browser and terminal consumers map every running=false sample, including STARTING and PAUSED, to a Stopped label.

The embedded dashboard listens at the host and port passed by main.py from its RuntimeSettings snapshot. start_dashboard_server and direct run_websocket_server calls retain static localhost:8765 defaults. A client receives products_list then state_update, and inbound JSON is dispatched by message type; browser/console endpoints remain independently selected.

One drain owner transitions to DRAINING and invokes hooks in order. The early OrderEngine hook blocks incomplete startup but preserves fully launched fill/event workers while the stealth producer stops; full engine cleanup then sets their stop event. The owner waits for tracked work and DRAINING-time hooks until one shared deadline, atomically closes registration, and marks logical STOPPED. Concurrent callers reuse the terminal result; bounded joins or timeout may leave cooperative daemon work exiting afterward.

Guarded status projection precedes strategy origination. The unified order-progress implementation converts cumulative WebSocket state to a delta, appends derived fill and audit data, and persists progress. When the ownership guard fails, the same factual path still runs but hotpoint and partial-fill follow-up origination are disabled.

FILLED processing first persists exact placement truth and its guarded logical execution owner. Only a complete projection reaches terminal follow-up handling; guard failure pauses and suppresses origination while factual fill accounting continues. Successful handling then claims work, resolves root/stealth ownership, persists exchange execution, applies external/accounting and durable-stop rules, and delegates shared root-strategy and percentage-threshold derivation to StealthOrderManager.

Every 30 seconds OrderEngine reads the flat order_parent table once, excludes terminal external rows, classifies unlinked roots first, validates each linked row points directly to a retained root, preserves persisted replacement counters and provenance, and atomically replaces the two disjoint compatibility maps only after the complete snapshot succeeds.

During STARTING the first pause request latches without changing state, complete_startup publishes PAUSED, and resume cannot open admission early. From RUNNING, pause changes state to PAUSED immediately; configured dashboard origins (including manual Rehide) and scheduler exchange actions remain blocked while cancellations, fills, queries, and admin controls continue. Actual transitions into RUNNING notify named admission-open hooks outside controller locks; the stealth bridge uses that edge to publish scheduler work only. Resume returns only PAUSED to RUNNING.
PeriodicReconciler waits its interval and repeats startup reconciliation with configured auto-heal/fill-audit policy until stopped.

main.py first loads a passive settings snapshot and explicitly composes one REST adapter, catalog, OrderBook, manager, bridge, engine, and dashboard adapter set. Startup then remains non-admitting while ordered stop hooks and signal handling precede passive stealth hydration and dashboard exposure; reconciliation or its explicit bypass, strict schedules, periodic registration, one-shot engine launch, and the initial fee attempt complete before readiness is published.

evidence.anchor: Importing this module performs no environment reads

summary: Importing configuration is passive. main.main explicitly loads environment and products.json into an immutable RuntimeSettings snapshot, constructs the REST adapter, prefers a live product catalog with cached fallback, loads positions fail-soft, and creates the sole shared OrderBook before wiring every runtime consumer.

OrderEngine claims one startup attempt, performs DB hydration and the synchronous initial fee-refresh attempt outside its lifecycle lock with stop checkpoints, and serializes only bounded worker/readiness publication against sticky stop. A partial launch calls retryable cooperative cleanup and never publishes readiness. Completion proves required non-fail-soft Thread.start calls and the fee attempt returned, not optional worker or fee success, complete hydration, worker health, websocket connection/subscription, or a first snapshot.

Startup reconciliation compares REST-open client_order_ids with nonterminal order_parent rows, classifies drift buckets, and auto-heals only exchange-closed/local-open rows; unknown-to-local and exchange-open/local-terminal remain operator review.

Bridge start strictly hydrates persisted stealth rows, including follow_up_reveal_direction with an opposite fallback for legacy rows, and starts only the 30-second reconciliation thread. Before decision schedules activate, it attempts exact recovery for hydrated pending_rearm intents; unresolved truth remains durable for the same reconciliation loop. After startup exchange/local reconciliation, or the explicit DISABLE_RECONCILER bypass, activate_decisions builds all derived schedules, starts the sole decision worker, then registers admission-open reconstruction; incomplete hydration, scheduling, worker activation, or hook registration fails closed. The 100ms cadence remains for active compatibility, admission, and overdue deadline/anchor retry rebuilding, but a non-admitting TRIGGERED row has no recurring admission retry.

The deadline worker marks anchor schedules due and the first eligible live ticker invokes the canonical manager path. HIDDEN repricing updates only local price/condition state. REVEALED repricing validates one fully accounted live placement, persists pending_rearm before cancellation, remains REVEALED, and creates no replacement. Matching authenticated zero-fill cancellation uses the guarded atomic status write to record distinct placement CANCELLED and logical PENDING states before restoring the slice to HIDDEN and setting reveal_armed_at. Fill or ambiguous identity fails closed. Recovery uses exact exchange truth and the same per-COID FIFO. Absolute price thresholds retain independent condition-path offsets, and root threshold edits propagate to current hidden/pending children while derived follow-ups rematerialize from persisted percentage context.
Condition evaluation selects price threshold, cumulative volume, time delay, spread, product ratio, or composite evaluators through get_evaluator; unknown condition types fall back to time delay.

The bridge reserves a root/follow-up client_order_id and holds its new-SID action lock through the manager transaction. The manager persists each new logical stealth order as its own execution owner. Follow-up creation first holds the source-SID lock and checks durable stop intent, while the creation lock serializes root-strategy resolution against edits. Canonical creation validates policy, price, size, and profitability; follow-ups inherit root strategy and derive mirrored percentage-distance thresholds around the final target.

Ordered product ticker events evaluate market/stable-time conditions through the per-order path; TIME_DELAY, ADMISSION_RETRY, and COMPATIBILITY_RECHECK deadline wakes use that same path. CONDITION_HOLD wakes await the next ordered market snapshot, while ANCHOR_REPRICE wakes publish the separate live-ticker handoff. Every condition PENDING/TRIGGERED transition must persist through one fail-closed boundary before lifecycle publication or reveal. Reveal placement uses atomic admission plus inflight registration, is deferred without recurring retry while pause owns admission, and retains snapshot-committed TRIGGERED state without condition re-evaluation. Admission-open publishes one immediate retry; generation fencing leaves one normal 100ms successor owner while active. Time-delay evaluation uses reveal_armed_at only after a confirmed REVEALED-to-HIDDEN rearm; ordinary hidden anchor movement does not restart that clock.

Manual stealth move, unlike automatic revealed rearming or Rehide, builds an eligibility/price plan, claims MOVE, cancels the active exchange order, pre-inserts a flat-root replacement row naming the logical SID as execution owner, places/classifies it, updates active pointers, and persists move audit.

The UI Rehide command targets the existing REVEALED identity and treats acceptance as pending withdrawal. Bridge admission/action locking and the manager REHIDE claim serialize it against MOVE/REPRICE. One fully accounted zero-fill placement enters the shared durable pending_rearm path; authenticated cancellation uses the atomic execution-owner guard before returning the logical row to PENDING/HIDDEN. It preserves configured price, conditions, sizing, linkage, cadence, and history, forces a fresh placement ID on re-reveal, and fails closed on fill evidence.

Every 30 seconds the bridge first reconciles persisted pending_rearm intents from exact venue truth, then queries active stealth IDs and loads only IDs missing from manager memory through the canonical lazy-load path, which publishes their derived schedules. Apart from same-ID rearm recovery, it neither refreshes changed cached rows nor evicts cached rows absent/terminal in DB.

Project cancellation durably records CANCELLED plus operator_cancel_requested_at before REST; that logical stop is not exchange closure. One provably tracked placement uses the existing terminal pending_rearm intent, superseding Rehide/reprice with return_to_hidden=false. Matching terminal truth is consumed through guarded atomic placement/logical status projection, including duplicates, instead of creating a cancellation replacement. Persistence failure, rejection, timeout, ambiguous identity, durable stop survival, source-SID origination guards, dashboard reporting, and unresolved-exposure retention remain fail-closed.

Reveal calculates and validates a strategy slice, normalizes the submission price, and pre-inserts each distinct placement row with flat strategy linkage plus the logical SID as execution owner before REST. It then runs placement hooks, performs post-only retries, classifies the response, and finalizes accepted or failed lifecycle state. This canonical path owns placement after cancel-to-HIDDEN rearm; neither repricing nor Rehide creates a replacement, and a completed rearm forces a fresh placement client_order_id.

The ticker worker publishes each admitted Coinbase snapshot to the stealth scheduler before other local handling. Accepted snapshots update current-state cache, dashboard, persistence, metrics, fee signals, and due anchor work; timestamp-stale snapshots enter the same FIFO as invalidation-only evidence and are suppressed from those downstream consumers.

For an unseen client_order_id, process_user_order creates an externally_created order_parent self-root before partial-fill-progress FK writes. Its NULL execution owner deliberately makes status projection exact-row-only. Active external rows rehydrate with provenance; terminal external handlers discard process-local claims and parent entries, and reconciliation does not reload them.

The sole private connection enters one instance-owned UserFeedProcessor, which retains channel, generation, connection-global sequence, timestamp, and all events through one bounded ordered reducer queue. Subscription acknowledgements, heartbeat, user, and futures messages share one generation watermark; the reducer drops stale/desynchronized work, isolates positions, and collects complete post-bootstrap PATCH/UPDATE rows for whole-envelope canonical dispatch.

Initial snapshot plus PATCH/UPDATE continuation pages accumulate by client_order_id until the first page below 50. Missing initial data and unterminated pagination each time out. Completion performs one drift check and one minimal in-memory hydration; bootstrap rows bypass process_user_order, database status writes, fill accounting, and follow-up creation.

UserFeedProcessor atomically admits complete canonical Coinbase orders to bounded FIFO lanes keyed by client_order_id. The single process_user_order path performs hooks, normalization, exchange-ID sync, parent assurance, guarded exact-placement/execution-owner projection and factual progress ingestion under the per-COID lock, then status routing, dashboard publication, and terminal eviction. Missing or conflicting owner evidence pauses and suppresses strategy/terminal origination without suppressing factual fill/audit writes. Recovered terminal truth uses the same FIFO and rearm tombstones suppress stale nonterminal replay.

Position members are generation-fenced and rejected after desynchronization, then processed independently before order reduction; shape or hook failure is logged without suppressing valid order work or changing the order bootstrap phase for a positions-only event.

Configured public channels use redundant WSClient-owned wrappers; user/futures-balance plus heartbeat use exactly one WSUserClient wrapper and an engine-owned reconnect generation. Every worker checks stop, subscribes only to its role channels, polls the SDK, and disconnects in finally after a connection attempt.

Public JSON uses EventBridge payload dedup and ticker-specific overflow recovery. Private JSON enters the instance-owned UserFeedProcessor, bypasses payload hashing, validates configured channels and complete envelopes against one connection-global sequence, retains generation/timestamp/channel, ignores only exact sequence replays, and desynchronizes plus reconnects on conflicts, gaps, malformed input, or bounded-queue overflow.
